name: Byron Bay Charters
description: Byron Bay Charters is based at Brunswick Heads, about 15 minutes north of Byron Bay, and runs fishing, whale watching, snorkelling and dive charters seven days a week, weather and bar conditions permitting. Fishing is done aboard Windarra, with a skipper and deckhand who each have more than 25 years of experience. Full-day trips leave the Brunswick Heads jetty at 6 am and return about 2 pm, with shorter trips on request, and can be set up for bottom fishing or for chasing pelagics. Catches include snapper, pearl perch, jewfish, kingfish, samsonfish and amberjack, with mackerel, wahoo, tuna and marlin in the warmer months. Quality rods and Wilson Live Fibre rods, bait, tackle, lunch, soft drinks, water and ice are included, and permits are provided. The business specialises in private and group bookings but can make up numbers for individuals.

Owner Mick McGillivray has worked his own commercial boats off Evans Head for more than 25 years and runs a 38 ft Randall customised for charter fishing, with skipper Simon named in recent reviews. Trips specialise in pearl perch and snapper in around 80 m of water about 30 km offshore, with jewfish, samsonfish, kingfish and teraglin also common. Individuals can book a six-hour trip, groups of up to ten can take the boat for six hours, and an eight-hour wide trip runs when the weather allows. Midweek packages combine a week of accommodation with three or five days of fishing, including optional afternoon jewfish sessions. Bait, tackle and the NSW fishing licence are supplied; bring food, drinks and an esky.

name: FishBermi Bermagui Fishing Charters

The boat is a 42 ft Randell flybridge cruiser in survey for 18 passengers and two crew, with a large private toilet and modern electronics, but shared trips are kept below nine anglers to leave plenty of room. Trips can be built around kingfish, a box of reef fish, yellowfin tuna, sharks or deep-water table fish such as gemfish and blue-eye trevalla, and multi-day bookings let groups mix it up. Private groups of up to twelve can hire the boat for reef, game or deep-sea days, and whale watching. The local crew help clean the catch, morning tea and drinks are supplied, breakfast or lunch can be arranged, and the vessel's licence covers anglers. Species include snapper, jewfish, kingfish, teraglin, morwong, flathead, trevally and John Dory, with mahi mahi in season. Ten-hour game charters for up to six chase marlin, yellowfin and albacore, with tag and release preferred. Seasonal whale watching is also offered.

Target species include snapper, flathead, kingfish, teraglin, jewfish, trevally, morwong and, in summer, mahi mahi and tuna. Shared trips suit individuals and pairs, private charters suit groups, and the Young Guns kids' trips are designed for families. Skipper Andy has more than a decade of charter experience. It suits groups wanting a big, stable boat for reef days as well as experienced anglers chasing pelagics off the shelf.

description: Sea Buoys Ocean Charters is skippered by Scott Wilson, who grew up on Lord Howe Island, fishes its waters commercially for island restaurants and has helped with kingfish satellite-tagging research. His boat, Fin, is a 9.4 m White Pointer Pro Sportsman in commercial survey, with a marine toilet and a marine park permit, and takes no more than six guests. Kingfish are the main event, best in winter, with yellowfin tuna, trevally and deep-water species also on offer. Trips are weather-led, with each week's schedule set on the Sunday before.

Shared four- and five-hour trips work the island shelf, and a five-hour shared trip runs to the Balls Pyramid area, while sole-use charters for up to four suit families and small groups. Jack fillets a feed of fish for guests, and extra catch is often taken up by island restaurants. The business also runs Mount Gower guided climbs and Balls Pyramid sightseeing and birding trips, so it suits visitors planning several island activities.

name: Fish Port Stephens Estuary Charters
description: Fish Port Stephens Estuary Charters is a dedicated estuary fishing charter owned and run by Paul Lennon, who has spent a lifetime fishing Port Stephens and knows its moods well. Trips stay inside the estuary, working weed beds, sand flats, rock walls, oyster racks, wrecks and deep holes in the main basin, and the Myall, Karuah and Tilligerry systems when the bay is choppy. description: Dundee Beach Fishing Charters is a locally based guiding business with about 25 years of experience fishing out of Dundee Beach, around 90 minutes from Darwin. Day charters leave the Dundee Beach ramp at 7am, or earlier if the tide suits, and run until about 3–4pm with a maximum of four clients per boat. Barra days fish the Finniss River and nearby coastal creeks with trolled and cast hard-bodies, soft plastics and Zerek fish traps, often finishing with a stop for jewfish. Reef days work inshore grounds for golden snapper, jewfish and cod, and wider grounds for red emperor, coral trout, bluebone and nannygai. Bluewater trips toward the Peron Islands and Bateman Shoals target queenfish, giant trevally, mackerel, tuna and sailfish. The boats are in 2C survey, with Shimano tackle, lunch and drinks supplied and the catch filleted. Multi-day packages include Darwin transfers, a chef and the company's air-conditioned Dundee Beach Retreat with a pool.

name: DNA Barra Fishing
description: DNA Barra Fishing (Darwin's North Australian Barra Fishing) is a family business started in 1995 by principal guide Duane Trouchet and his father Greg, who have fished the Territory since 1980. It is one of the few guiding businesses licensed to fish inside Kakadu National Park. In the March–May run-off it runs extended trips of 2 to 14 days on the South and East Alligator Rivers, staying at Aurora Kakadu in Jabiru, with golden snapper and black jewfish on the reefs off the river mouths when the tides ease. It also runs build-up trips to an island camp on Endyalgout Island in western Arnhem Land. Closer to Darwin there are day trips to Corroboree Billabong, Shady Camp and Darwin Harbour, where barra, queenfish, longtail tuna and mackerel are on offer. Guests are picked up in air-conditioned Landcruisers and fish four to a boat from custom alloy barra boats with swivel seats and shade. G-Loomis rods, Shimano reels and lunch are supplied.

name: Kakadu Fishing Tours
description: Kakadu Fishing Tours is a family-owned guiding business based in Jabiru that fishes only inside Kakadu National Park, one of a small number of operators approved to guide there. In the dry season (June to October) it runs three short trips a day on the East Alligator River above Cahill's Crossing, a scenic stretch beneath the Arnhem Land escarpment where both freshwater and saltwater barramundi are caught. The business's record fish there measured 135cm. In the March–May run-off it switches to full-day and multi-day charters on the big Kakadu rivers, including the South Alligator floodplains, and can arrange Jabiru accommodation or a mothership stay on the East Alligator. Groups are capped at four on a custom 6m plate-aluminium barra boat with a 175hp Suzuki and electric trolling motor. Shimano tackle, soft drinks and water are supplied. Pick-up is from Jabiru accommodation, and guides help both newcomers and experienced anglers.

name: Estuary Escapes Fishing Charters
description: Estuary Escapes is a small owner-operated guiding business run by Brian and Di Hutchinson, with Brian, an accredited fishing guide, at the helm. From late February to May the business is based at Shady Camp on the Mary River, chasing run-off barramundi with trolling and casting when big fish gather to feed on bait flushed off the floodplains. For the rest of the season, to early December, Brian runs day and multi-day trips from Darwin. Destinations include Darwin and Bynoe Harbours, Dundee Beach, the Adelaide and Finniss Rivers and Corroboree Billabong, where saratoga, tarpon and sooty grunter add variety. The boat, MV Reel Escape, is a 6.1m Sea Adex Typhoon 6 built to 2D survey, with LiveScope, an electric motor with GPS anchoring, shade and a porta-potty. It takes up to four guests. Day trips include Darwin pick-up, morning tea, lunch and all tackle, and beginners get coaching on technique.

name: Just Doon It Fishing Charters
description: Just Doon It is a Humpty Doo-based barramundi guiding business run by Jayson ('Capt'n Doon') and Kate, who also host a campground. Jayson holds an NT Fishing Tour Operator licence and Coxswain certificate. Fishing focuses on three areas: Shady Camp on the Mary River, the Daly River and the tidal creeks around Dundee Beach. In the March–May run-off the business runs multi-day trips, including mothership trips with an onboard cook, accommodation and transfers from Darwin. Through the dry season (about May to November) it offers shared and private one-day trips, and mothership trips also run around the Tiwi Islands in the build-up. The barra boat, 'Saltie', carries a maximum of four anglers. The style is sight-casting and lure fishing tight to structure, and the business practises catch and release while letting groups keep a legal feed. Lunch, snacks, soft drinks, quality rods, reels and lures, and filleting are included. No experience is needed.

name: Point Stuart Wilderness Lodge
description: Point Stuart Wilderness Lodge sits in the Mary River wetlands, about two hours' drive from Darwin on a mostly sealed road and 20 minutes from Shady Camp. Besides accommodation, the lodge holds an NT Fishing Tour Operator licence and runs guided barramundi trips with local guides who have lived and fished on the Mary River for over two decades. Half-day trips leave the Shady Camp boat ramp in the early morning or afternoon from mid-May to early October. Full-day trips, available as 1 to 5 days for guests who drive in, leave the lodge early and run from late February to early October, covering the run-off and dry season. Guides fish from purpose-built surveyed alloy boats and tailor each day to casting, trolling with hard-bodies and soft plastics, or fly fishing, with tuition for newcomers. Lunch, drinks, ice and quality tackle are included on full days. The lodge also offers self-drive boat hire, cruises and wildlife tours.

name: Alure Fishing Charters NT
description: Alure Fishing Charters NT is owned and run by Gerard Wilkie, who has fished the Territory for more than 30 years. Before starting the business he skippered the Mandorah and Tiwi Islands ferry and worked as a skipper for two Darwin charter companies. Its signature trip is a full day to the Tiwi Islands: guests meet at Dinah Beach, launch from Leaders Creek and run past the Vernon Islands and the Adelaide River mouth. Golden snapper and black jewfish are the year-round targets there, with queenfish, trevally and Spanish mackerel added in the dry season. The same 7.5m Ocean Cylinder, with twin 150hp Hondas, a hard top and an electric spot-lock motor, also runs Darwin Harbour reef trips, Dundee Beach and Peron Islands days, offshore bluewater trips, and barramundi trips to the Adelaide, Daly and Mary River systems. Shared trips take up to four to six anglers. Tackle, bait and soft drinks are included, with lunch on full days.

name: Tiwi Island Retreat
description: Tiwi Island Retreat is a beachfront fly-in lodge at Port Hurd on the western edge of Bathurst Island, about 30 minutes by charter flight from Darwin. Guests are met at the Port Hurd airstrip and taken across by boat. Its all-inclusive Fishing Adventure package runs three nights and four days. It includes a guided bluewater charter for reef fish such as golden snapper, black jewfish, coral trout and red emperor, plus a guided estuary charter for barramundi in the island's tidal creeks, with beach-buggy fishing at sunset. In the dry season, longtail tuna, cobia, queenfish and trevally are common offshore. Packages cover return flights from Darwin, Tiwi visitor and fishing permits, fishing tackle, all meals and drinks, with accommodation ranging from village rooms to ocean-view rooms and glamping tents. The retreat closes for the wet season (December to March). It suits couples, families and groups who want guided fishing combined with a comfortable island stay and Tiwi cultural experiences.
